pred_ddx.label: Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head

Chronic Osteomyelitis: The patient's symptoms of progressive hip pain, night pain, and weight loss, along with the MRI findings of a T1-hypointense, STIR-hyperintense lesion with a thick sclerotic rim in the femoral head, are consistent with chronic osteomyelitis. The lack of response to empirical anti-tubercular therapy and the presence of chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates on biopsy also support this diagnosis.
Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head: The patient's symptoms of hip pain and the MRI findings of a well-defined lesion in the femoral head with associated marrow edema and synovitis are also consistent with avascular necrosis of the femoral head. The patient's lack of response to empirical anti-tubercular therapy and the presence of chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates on biopsy do not rule out this diagnosis.
